name: Kori Gassi (Mangalorean Chicken Curry)
instructions: 1. Dry roast coriander, cumin, fenugreek, peppercorns, and red chilies until fragrant, then grind them with grated coconut, garlic, and tamarind to a smooth paste.
2. In a pan, heat coconut oil and sauté half the chopped onions and curry leaves until golden brown.
3. Add the chicken pieces and turmeric, cooking until the chicken turns pale.
4. Add the prepared coconut masala paste and enough water to reach desired consistency.
5. Simmer on low heat until the chicken is tender and the oil separates on the surface.
6. Temper with remaining onions fried in a little coconut oil before serving hot.
description: Kori Gassi is a quintessential dish from the Bunt community of Mangalore. 'Kori' means chicken and 'Gassi' means curry. It is a staple at traditional celebrations and is most popularly paired with Neer Dosa or Pundi (rice dumplings), reflecting the coastal heritage of the Tulu Nadu region.
